title: Rigveda 10.77: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.77: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.77 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 43r-44r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.77.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 43r
translation.original_text:
1a̱bhra̱pruṣo̱ na vā̱cā pru̍ṣā̱ vasu̍ ha̱viṣma̍nto̱ na ya̱jñā vi̍jā̱nuṣa̍ḥ | su̱māru̍ta̱ṁ na bra̱hmāṇa̍m a̱rhase̍ ga̱ṇam a̍stoṣy eṣā̱ṁ na śo̱bhase̍ ||
2śri̱ye maryā̍so a̱ñjīm̐r a̍kṛṇvata su̱māru̍ta̱ṁ na pū̱rvīr ati̱ kṣapa̍ḥ | di̱vas pu̱trāsa̱ etā̱ na ye̍tira ādi̱tyāsa̱s te a̱krā na vā̍vṛdhuḥ ||
3pra ye di̱vaḥ pṛ̍thi̱vyā na ba̱rhaṇā̱ tmanā̍ riri̱cre a̱bhrān na sūrya̍ḥ | pāja̍svanto̱ na vī̱rāḥ pa̍na̱syavo̍ ri̱śāda̍so̱ na maryā̍ a̱bhidya̍vaḥ ||
translation.text:
1As with their voice from cloud they sprinkle treasure so are the wise man's liberal sacrifices. I praise their Company that merits worship as the good Martits' priest to pay them honour.
2The youths have wrought their ornaments for glory through many nights,– this noble band of Maruts. Like stags the Sons of Dyaus have striven onward, the Sons of Aditi grown strong like pillars.
3They who extend beyond the earth and heaven, by their own mass, as from the cloud spreads Sûrya; Like mighty Heroes covetous of glory, like heavenly gallants who destroy the wicked.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 43r (numbered 42r by the scribe) (OPenn image 42, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.76.8 ‹-svapaso abhūtana ya indrāya›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 43v (numbered 42v by the scribe), begins in RV 10.77.4 ‹yuṣmākam budhne apāṁ na›. Verses 10.77.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.77.4-6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 10); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 43v
translation.original_text:
4yu̱ṣmāka̍m bu̱dhne a̱pāṁ na yāma̍ni vithu̱ryati̱ na ma̱hī śra̍tha̱ryati̍ | vi̱śvapsu̍r ya̱jño a̱rvāg a̱yaṁ su va̱ḥ praya̍svanto̱ na sa̱trāca̱ ā ga̍ta ||
5yū̱yaṁ dhū̱rṣu pra̱yujo̱ na ra̱śmibhi̱r jyoti̍ṣmanto̱ na bhā̱sā vyu̍ṣṭiṣu | śye̱nāso̱ na svaya̍śaso ri̱śāda̍saḥ pra̱vāso̱ na prasi̍tāsaḥ pari̱pruṣa̍ḥ ||
6pra yad vaha̍dhve marutaḥ parā̱kād yū̱yam ma̱haḥ sa̱ṁvara̍ṇasya̱ vasva̍ḥ | vi̱dā̱nāso̍ vasavo̱ rādhya̍syā̱rāc ci̱d dveṣa̍ḥ sanu̱tar yu̍yota ||
translation.text:
4When ye come nigh, as in the depth of waters, the earth is loosened, as it were, and shaken. This your all-feedin sacrifice approaches: come all united, fraught, as 'twere with viands.
5Ye are like horses fastened to the chariot poles, luminous with your beams, with splendour as at dawn; Like self-bright falcons, punishers of wicked men, like hovering birds urged forward, scattering rain around.
6When ye come forth, O Maruts, from the distance, from the great treasury of rich possessions, Knowing, O Vasus, boons that should be granted, even from afar drive back the men who hate us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 43v (numbered 42v by the scribe) (OPenn image 43, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.77.4 ‹yuṣmākam budhne apāṁ na›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 44r (numbered 43r by the scribe), begins in RV 10.77.7 ‹-devānām api gopīthe astu›. Verses 10.77.4-6 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.77.7-8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 44r
translation.original_text:
7ya u̱dṛci̍ ya̱jñe a̍dhvare̱ṣṭhā ma̱rudbhyo̱ na mānu̍ṣo̱ dadā̍śat | re̱vat sa vayo̍ dadhate su̱vīra̱ṁ sa de̱vānā̱m api̍ gopī̱the a̍stu ||
8te hi ya̱jñeṣu̍ ya̱jñiyā̍sa̱ ūmā̍ ādi̱tyena̱ nāmnā̱ śambha̍viṣṭhāḥ | te no̍ 'vantu ratha̱tūr ma̍nī̱ṣām ma̱haś ca̱ yāma̍nn adhva̱re ca̍kā̱nāḥ ||
translation.text:
7He who, engaged in the rite's final duty brings, as a man, oblation to the Maruts, Wins him life's wealthy fulness, blest with heroes: he shall be present, too, where Gods drink Soma.
8For these are helps adored at sacrifices, bringing good fortune by their name Âdityas. Speeding on cars let them protect our praises, delighting in our sacrifice and worship.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 44r (numbered 43r by the scribe) (OPenn image 43, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.77.7 ‹-devānām api gopīthe astu›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 44v (numbered 43v by the scribe), begins in RV 10.78.3 ‹-virokiṇaḥ›. Verses 10.77.7-8 end on this page; 10.77.7 begins on fol. 43v (numbered 42v by the scribe).
